paper.title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling
paper.central_claim: Building an offline replay environment lets an explorer LLM (Claude Code) iteratively synthesize width-depth test-time-scaling controllers as code using scaling-curve and execution-trace feedback and a single beta knob; the discovered controller improves the accuracy-cost tradeoff over handcrafted TTS baselines, generalizes to held-out benchmarks/model scales, and costs only $39.9 and 160 minutes to find.

signatures.object: Code-defined width-depth TTS controller (OptimalController class with beta schedule and trace hooks) for a frozen base LLM; baseline = handcrafted ASC/ESC/Parallel-Probe/SC@64
signatures.information: Explorer sees the environment API, seed baselines, full history of prior controllers, their beta-sweep scaling curves and per-question decision traces; replay environment hides gold answers from the controller; controllers see probe answers only when probing
signatures.operation: Explorer LLM (Claude Code) rewrites the controller from a template each round after reading history; controller evaluated on offline replay of AIME24 for four Qwen3 models
signatures.output: Executable controller class + beta-to-hyperparameter map; final = highest AIME24 accuracy over rounds and beta
signatures.conditions: pre-sampled 128 trajectories per (model, problem), 500-token probe interval, 64 resampled evaluations per controller, 5 rounds
signatures.feedback: accuracy-token scaling curve across beta sweep; execution traces of branch/probe/prune/stop decisions
signatures.selection_rule_data: highest accuracy on search environments (AIME24); held-out AIME25/HMMT25 not used (author claim); no population, no parent sampling
signatures.persistence: history archive of rounds (code, CSV results, JSONL traces); final controller released as code
signatures.later_use: fixed controller run on held-out benchmarks and other models via replay
signatures.claimed_effect: average held-out token saving about 69.5% vs SC@64 at on-par accuracy (beta=0.5); peak accuracy beyond handcrafted in 5 of 8 cases (beta=1.0)
signatures.failure_boundary: single discovery run, one frontier explorer, replay fidelity unvalidated, probing treated as cheap, only width-depth action set

signatures.object: Search space parameterization: each controller exposes one monotone scalar beta mapped to all internal hyperparameters
signatures.operation: Discovery prompt requires single-knob schedule; map produced by the coding agent
signatures.output: 1-D sweep that traces an accuracy-cost frontier
signatures.conditions: controller must be expressible with a monotone beta schedule
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o beta: 6x fewer tokens, held-out acc 49.0 vs 53.1
signatures.failure_boundary: discovered CMC still has 12 internal hyperparameters via hand-chosen linear schedules; no iso-cost comparison

gap.author_gap: TTS strategies are hand-designed heuristics tuned by intuition; evaluating candidate strategies online is too expensive for automated search, and scalar feedback does not tell the explorer why a controller fails.
gap.checked_gap: Real but partly generic: hand-designed controllers exist, and expensive evaluation is a concrete bottleneck that replay addresses. Not established: that LLM-agent code search finds better controllers than a cheap automated tuning of the existing controllers on the same replay data; that baseline hyperparameters were optimal; that the space is meaningfully unexplored.

domain_pattern.reason: Opus. H14 is primary: its genome list names control policies, step 1 prescribes replay or proxy evaluators when live evaluation is expensive, and step 3 grounds mutations in evaluator traces, which is AutoTTS's design. H17 is kept as secondary: offline search over executable inference-time workflow code, one frozen design deployed and certified on held-out sets. son55's H12 (low) is dropped: there is no incumbent patching or promote/rollback, and the template is reset each round.
revision_proposals: son55: a domain-card note for inference-time algorithm discovery on offline replay environments under H14/H15.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: The TTS design problem becomes a replay MDP, and an LLM explorer proposes controller code that the deterministic replay evaluator scores. The best search-set controller is retained and frozen.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions: Pre-collected trajectories and probe answers; a single-knob interface.
pattern_mapping.differences: History archive rather than parent sampling; no replay-to-live fidelity check.

claims.text: Discovered controller improves the accuracy-cost tradeoff over handcrafted TTS baselines on held-out benchmarks
claims.setting: Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B/4B/8B, replay of AIME25 and HMMT25 (30 problems each)
claims.baseline_control: SC@64, ASC, ESC, Parallel-Probe at original settings
claims.result_denominator: avg held-out: beta=1.0 acc 24.6/40.6/60.5/62.7 vs best baseline 24.1/34.3/60.4/62.8; beta=0.5 tokens ~254k-379k vs SC@64 ~0.9-1.2M
counterevidence: ASC dominates on Qwen3-4B and is close on 8B in token cost; margins of 0.1-0.5 acc points are inside noise on 30 problems; baselines untuned.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Discovered controller is competitive with strong baselines and clearly better than SC@64 on tokens; superiority over best handcrafted is shown only for small models.

claims.text: Discovered strategies generalize to held-out benchmarks and other model families
claims.setting: R1-Distill-Llama-8B on HMMT25; Qwen3-1.7B on GPQA-Diamond
claims.result_denominator: 27.2 vs 26.7 acc at 533.9K vs 985.7K tokens; GPQA 41.6 vs 41.3 at 151K vs 510K
claims.counterevidence: One model-benchmark pair each, tiny accuracy deltas, no repeats.
claims.allowed_conclusion: No evidence of failure out of distribution; weak evidence of transfer.

claims.text: Beta parameterization and execution traces are needed for effective discovery
claims.counterevidence: Different operating points, single run, no search-cost-matched comparison.

claims.allowed_conclusion: Agent-API cost of the loop is small; total pipeline cost not shown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A Claude Code-written controller selected on AIME24 replay achieves, on replayed AIME25/HMMT25, roughly 40-70% fewer tokens than SC@64 with on-par accuracy (author-reported), and beats the handcrafted baselines on accuracy for the 0.6B and 1.7B models.
assessment.not_supported: Superiority over tuned or ASC-style cost-efficient baselines on 4B/8B; benefit of agentic search over simpler automated tuning; fidelity of replay to live generation including probe cost; reproducibility across discovery runs; total pipeline cost.
unresolved: Opus: the Figure 3 'consistently stronger frontier' is not borne out at 4B/8B against ASC in Table 1 (opus:O01).
Opus: Table 3's Avg includes the search set (sol:E016).
assessment.note: Author-reported results only. Improver level not claimed: the explorer is not improved.

G.reason: Opus = sol. The bottleneck is concrete and partly demonstrated: online evaluation of candidate allocation policies is too costly (answered by replay), many free hyperparameters overfit (the paper's preliminary finding and the w/o-β row), and scalar feedback does not explain failures (the w/o-traces row). The TTS lineage (SC/ASC/ESC/Parallel-Probe) is compared empirically; the discovery lineage (FunSearch/ADAS/AlphaEvolve/Meta-Harness) is named, with the inherited trace idea acknowledged. Not 4: the 'first algorithmic-search formulation of TTS' and the 'unexplored space' are asserted, not checked. son55's missing automated-tuning alternative is an E.causality control (A2 rule) and is scored there.

M.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. Replay MDP → code candidates → trace-augmented history → single-β schedule → search-set selection → frozen reuse is reconstructable and answers the stated problems. Weak points: β's anti-overfit role rests on a preliminary observation, and the schedule fans out to 12 hand-set forms.

X.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. The prompt, environment API, replay protocol, selection rule and full controller code are disclosed. Not 4: the explorer version and seed, and the β grid, are unspecified; there is no promotion gate beyond search accuracy; there are docstring/code mismatches (the ema_alpha comment, a non-existent burst_senior).

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed. Accuracy against ground truth and total branch tokens target the claim, but everything is replay on 30-problem sets. Probing is treated as free, which favours probe-based methods over full-read ASC/ESC. Table 3's 'Avg' includes the search set but is called held-out (sol:E017). The figure-only frontier claim is not borne out at 4B/8B against ASC in Table 1 (opus:O01).

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed. There are handcrafted baselines and w/o-β and w/o-traces discovery ablations. The w/o-β arm sits at a 6× lower token budget (not iso-cost). The ablations are single discovery runs. There is no matched-effort tuning of the baselines, no non-LLM or random search control, and no per-mechanism ablation of CMC.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 3, confirmed. Selection is on AIME24 replay; AIME25/HMMT25 are never used for discovery or selection; R1-Distill-Llama-8B and GPQA are extra transfer tests. Not 4: all four Qwen sizes are in the search union, so 'across model scales' is not unseen-scale evidence; held-out curves were tracked per round; the held-out sets are near-distribution.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1, confirmed (A2 tier 1). Sample sizes (30-problem sets, a 128-trajectory pool, 64 subsample draws) and dominated or negative points are shown, but there is no spread, interval or test, and only one discovery run.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 2, confirmed. Discovery $39.9/160 min and the ablation search costs are reported, and inference tokens are central. The pre-sampling of 128 trajectories per model–problem and live probing costs are excluded, and baseline effort is not matched.

aggregate_review.initial_judgment_before_seat_scores: Read the full text first. A clean held-out benchmark split and a frozen code artifact, but replay-only measurement, no variance, ASC-dominated points at 4B/8B, an Avg that mixes in the search set, and partial cost accounting. Expected low-to-mid 60s.
